name: Stratholme
summary: Scourge forces hold Stratholme, and its ruins still burn. Once the jewel of the Eastweald and Lordaeron’s second greatest city, it became the place where Prince Arthas Menethil ordered the culling of citizens who had eaten grain tainted by the Plague of Undeath.

sections.title: Cradle of Paladins and Trade
sections.body:
Stratholme rose with the Arathi expansion into the Eastweald centuries ago. It became Lordaeron’s second-largest settlement, famed for holy shrines and sacred water that resisted dark sorcery. Before the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol gathered at the city’s chapel and founded the Order of the Knights of the Silver Hand.

Among its first legends was Uther the Lightbringer. During the Second War, Stratholme served the Alliance of Lordaeron as a vital port, supply hub, and northern oil refinery. The Old Horde assaulted it, but victory brought the city’s rebuilding.

sections.title: The Culling and Eternal Ruin
sections.body:
The Cult of the Damned carried infected grain from Andorhal into Stratholme’s markets. Unaware of the taint, thousands ate the flour. Prince Arthas arrived with Uther and Jaina Proudmoore, but the infection had spread too far to cure.

He judged slaughter the only way to deny Mal'Ganis an entire army and ordered every citizen killed. The atrocity drove Uther and Jaina away and began the prince’s descent into madness. His forces set the city ablaze. Then the Scourge took its smoking ruins for their regional capital.

faq.answer: During the Third War, Prince Arthas’s forces set Stratholme’s homes and streets ablaze to kill the infected and halt the spread of undeath. The plague-tainted fire has burned ever since, fed by dark necromantic energies and the Scourge infestation.

faq.q: What was the Culling of Stratholme?
faq.answer: The Culling of Stratholme was Prince Arthas Menethil’s slaughter of the city’s people. After they ate grain infected with the Plague of Undeath, he ordered every inhabitant killed, sick or healthy, before they could rise as Scourge soldiers. His choice broke his alliances and his moral compass.

faq.q: What historic role did Stratholme play for the Silver Hand?
aliases: order of the silver hand stratholme
faq.answer: Archbishop Alonsus Faol founded the Knights of the Silver Hand in Stratholme’s Alonsus Chapel before the Second War. He anointed its first five members, including Uther the Lightbringer, Turalyon, and Saidan Dathrohan.

faq.q: What happened to Tirion Fordring here?
faq.answer: Years after the Second War, Lord Tirion Fordring stood trial for treason in Stratholme’s Hall of Justice after defending the honorable orc hermit Eitrigg. Uther and Alliance leaders judged him, stripped him of his title, and exiled him. Tirion later freed Eitrigg during an attack on the city led by Thrall.

angles.text: As a paladin, you can look to Stratholme as hallowed ground turned tragic. The Order of the Silver Hand began here, and Arthas shattered that brotherhood when he demanded the slaughter of innocent citizens.
As an Alliance traveler, you see a ruined city that recalls Lordaeron’s fall and the heavy price the northern kingdoms paid to plague and treachery.
